learning_objectives.statement: Identify and correctly name 16 core immediate and extended family members in spoken and written English when presented with a 3-generation family tree.
Accurately apply collective plural terms (parents, grandparents, siblings, children, relatives) to group family members in natural sentence frames.
Differentiate relational kinship pairs (uncle vs aunt, nephew vs niece, cousin) without transferring Vietnamese age/lineage over-specifications, solving family logic riddles within 3 seconds.

core_concepts: Generational Tiers (Gen 1: Grandparents -> Gen 2: Parents/Uncles/Aunts -> Gen 3: Self/Siblings/Cousins)
target_linguistic_structures: This is my [singular noun]. / These are my [plural noun].

key_terminology.definition_for_learner: The father of your father or mother.
The mother of your father or mother.
The parents of your parents (both grandfather and grandmother together).
A boy or man who has the same parents as you.
A girl or woman who has the same parents as you.
Brothers and sisters who share the same parents.
The brother of your mother or father.
The sister of your mother or father.
The child of your uncle or aunt (boy or girl).
The son of your brother or sister.
The daughter of your brother or sister.

prerequisite_knowledge.concept: Personal Pronouns (I, he, she, they, we)
prerequisite_knowledge.remediation_if_missing: Explicit color-coded avatars on whiteboard (Blue=He, Teal=She, Yellow/Multi=They).
Use arrow labels: 'Liam -> Liam's father -> his father'.
Visual bracket grouping singular items into a plural label (1 parent + 1 parent = 2 parents).

nodes.concept_name: Generation 3D: Nephew & Niece (Viewed from Liam's perspective as an uncle)

concept_structure.explanation: A central 3-tier family tree with Liam at Gen 3 center. Connectors show biological descent; horizontal brackets show marriage/partners and sibling groups; colored boxes demonstrate collective plural terms.

common_misconceptions.erroneous_belief: Believing English must have distinct words for older vs younger uncle/aunt or maternal vs paternal relatives (like Vietnamese bác, chú, cô, dì, cậu, thím, mợ).
common_misconceptions.l1_interference_factor: Vietnamese kinship system is strictly stratified by seniority and lineage.
common_misconceptions.pedagogical_antidote: The 'Universal Umbrella' visual technique: Show 4 diverse Vietnamese relatives (bác trai, chú, cậu) all walking under ONE large umbrella labeled 'UNCLE'.

common_misconceptions.erroneous_belief: Confusing 'nephew' and 'niece' or forgetting which gender each refers to.
common_misconceptions.l1_interference_factor: In Vietnamese, both are called 'cháu' and need a trailing modifier 'trai/gái'. English uses two entirely different Latin roots.
common_misconceptions.pedagogical_antidote: Phonetic & visual mnemonic: N**E**PHEW has 'E' like H**E** (boy). NI**ECE** has 'C' like S**HE** (girl) and sounds like a piece of sweet candy.

common_misconceptions.erroneous_belief: Saying 'cousin brother' or 'cousin sister' to specify gender.
common_misconceptions.l1_interference_factor: Direct translation from Vietnamese 'anh họ', 'chị họ', 'em họ'.
common_misconceptions.pedagogical_antidote: A red strike-through marker crossing out 'cousin brother' on the whiteboard with an alert note: 'In English, COUSIN is always gender-neutral! Just say COUSIN.'.

common_misconceptions.erroneous_belief: Pronouncing 'father, mother, brother' with a hard /d/ ('fader') or /z/ ('fazer').
common_misconceptions.l1_interference_factor: Vietnamese phonology lacks the voiced dental fricative /ð/.
common_misconceptions.pedagogical_antidote: Visual animated lip/teeth diagram showing tongue tip touching the upper teeth lightly with vibrating voice icon.

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: Activate curiosity with a family photo album and introduce Liam's quest to draw his family tree.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Establish context, lower affective filter, and introduce the 3-generation canvas structure.

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: Father, Mother, Parents, Brother, Sister, Siblings, Son, Daughter, Children.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Anchor the immediate core family and master the 2 essential collective brackets (Parents, Siblings).
Establish Generation 1, teach the 'grand-' prefix pattern, and contrast with 'parents'.
Debunk Vietnamese over-complication with the Universal Umbrella and resolve the Nephew/Niece gender challenge.

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: The /ð/ sound in father/mother/brother, and final /s/, /z/ endings in parents/cousins.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Phonological precision check to prevent fossilized pronunciation errors.

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: Flash Quiz: 'Who is this?' with a 3-second hand countdown.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Formative retrieval practice under timed condition; active recall of immediate kinship terms.

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: The Family Detective: Deductive logic riddle on the tree.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Deductive cognitive processing; tests relational comprehension (e.g. My father's brother's daughter = my cousin).

teaching_sequence.instructional_focus: Full family tree summary anchor with color-coded memory takeaway.
teaching_sequence.pedagogical_intent: Long-term memory consolidation and celebration of mastery.

positive_examples: John and Mary are Liam's parents.
negative_counter_examples: Liam's uncle and aunt are his parents. (FALSE: They are relatives, not parents!)
Liam has three parents. (FALSE: In standard biological kinship, you have two parents.)
examples_and_non_examples.boundary_distinction_note: Parents refers EXCLUSIVELY to father and mother together.

positive_examples: Liam has two siblings: one brother and one sister.
negative_counter_examples: Liam and his cousins are siblings. (FALSE: Cousins are not siblings!)
My dog and I are siblings. (FALSE: Siblings must be human children sharing the same parents.)
examples_and_non_examples.boundary_distinction_note: Siblings strictly refers to brothers and sisters who share the same parents.

positive_examples: Sarah is Liam's cousin. She is 12 years old.
David is also Liam's cousin. He is 20 years old.
negative_counter_examples: Sarah is Liam's cousin sister. (INCORRECT: In English, never say 'cousin sister' or 'cousin brother'!)
Sarah is Liam's aunt. (FALSE: Aunt is the parent's sister, cousin is the aunt's child.)
examples_and_non_examples.boundary_distinction_note: 'Cousin' is completely gender-neutral and age-neutral in English.

positive_examples: Liam has one nephew (his brother's son) and one niece (his sister's daughter).
negative_counter_examples: Liam has a female nephew. (FALSE: A nephew is ALWAYS male!)
Liam's brother's son is his cousin. (FALSE: Brother's son is nephew, not cousin!)
examples_and_non_examples.boundary_distinction_note: Nephew = Male child of sibling; Niece = Female child of sibling.

visual_analogies: The Universal Kinship Umbrella: One English word covers multiple Vietnamese titles.
The Tree Branching Analogy: Generations stacked vertically like tree tiers.
The Orange Collective Brackets: Uniting individual members into collective nouns.
decision_rules_for_learner: If it's the child of your brother/sister: Boy = Nephew, Girl = Niece.
If it's the brother/sister of your parents: Male = Uncle, Female = Aunt.
If it's the child of your uncle/aunt: Always COUSIN (no gender suffix!).
If they are both your father and mother: PARENTS (with final -s!).

sample_questions.prompt: Look at the tree: Lisa is Liam's sister. John is their father. What is Lisa to John?
sample_questions.feedback_explanation: Correct! Lisa is John's DAUGHTER, and Liam is John's SON!

sample_questions.prompt: Riddle Time: 'My father has a brother named Tom. Uncle Tom has a son named Lucas. Who is Lucas to me?'
sample_questions.feedback_explanation: Brilliant! Your uncle's son is your COUSIN!

forbidden_extensions: No distant multi-tier relatives (great-grandparents, second cousins)
deferred_to_future_lessons: Marital status vocabulary (married, divorced, single, widowed)
Describing physical appearances and personality traits of family members
